name: OX Quiz Widget
description: A mobile-friendly OX (True/False) quiz widget for educational apps that shows one question at a time, gives instant feedback, and tracks progress.

requirement.summary: An OX quiz interface for an educational mobile app. The user answers questions one at a time by choosing O or X and receives the correct answer with an explanation, along with progress tracking and a retry option.
details: Display a list of OX quiz questions one at a time from a predefined question set (each question has text, a correct answer of O or X, and an explanation)
Provide O and X answer buttons for the user to select an answer
After selection, lock further input for the current question and show whether the answer is correct, the correct answer, and an explanation
Show progress as completed/total questions (e.g., '3/10 문제 완료') with a visual progress bar
Provide a 'Next' action to move to the following question after feedback is shown
Show a completion summary when all questions are answered, including the score (number of correct answers out of total)
Provide a 'Retry' (다시 풀기) function that resets all state and restarts the quiz from the first question

Component structure: QuizContainer (overall quiz layout and state owner), QuestionCard (current question display), AnswerButtons (O/X selection buttons), ProgressBar (progress indicator), ResultDisplay (correct/incorrect feedback with explanation)
Manage state for: current question index, user answers, correctness of each answer, and quiz completion status
Responsive design optimized for mobile and tablet screen sizes, with large touch-friendly buttons
Transition animations when showing feedback and moving between questions, using Tailwind transition/animation utilities

Accessibility: full keyboard navigation (Tab focus order, Enter/Space to activate buttons, optional O/X key shortcuts), visible focus states, aria-labels on buttons, aria-live region announcing correct/incorrect results, and progress exposed via role='progressbar' with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemax
Color scheme: green for correct answers, red for incorrect answers, gray for neutral/unanswered states
Use the system default font stack (Tailwind font-sans), with no external fonts
Styling uses Tailwind CSS only, with no custom CSS files or inline style objects
